name: b-over-the-nurse-shoulder
prompt: An old-fashioned newspaper cartoon drawn with a dip pen and India ink, loose confident outlines and tight parallel hatching, tinted with a thin cool blue-grey watercolour wash on cream paper. We look past a hospital nurse from just behind her: the lower edge of the picture holds the soft, out-of-focus curve of her shoulder in pale scrubs and the knot of her tied-back hair, drawn in a few faint unfinished strokes. Filling the centre of the tall frame is the man beside her on a park bench, a heavy, well-fed gentleman of a century ago in a glossy silk top hat, starched wing collar and fat cravat, his jowls spilling over the collar. He is halfway through brushing her off: heavy eyelids drooping almost closed, mouth turned down around a thick cigar clamped at one corner, one gloved hand lifted with the palm turned up toward her in a lazy, bored shrug. It is just after dawn at the end of a night shift; a weak, low sun sits behind him, so a bright thin line of light traces the brim and crown of his hat and the edge of his shoulders while his face falls into hatched shadow. Far behind, small and sketched with only a few thin lines, a cluster of modern glass office towers catches the same pale light. The upper third of the picture is open, empty morning sky with only the faintest wash, kept clear for a caption to be added later. The drawing itself carries no writing of any kind: no lettering, labels, speech balloons or artist's mark. Thanks.
